forecast.note: Walk-forward, out-of-sample. Beats the naive baseline so far. Direction forecasts for indices are rarely much better than a coin flip; this is context, not a trade trigger.

contagion.note: Correlation and Granger tests measure statistical association and predictive precedence on past daily data. They are not proof of cause and they change over time.

anomalies.note: Statistical outliers vs each symbol's own 60-day history (and its sector). Context for investigation, not trade signals.

ml.label: 10-session forward return > 1%
ml.note: SHADOW MODE: ranks stocks, never trades. Has NOT met the promotion rule; rule scanner stays in charge.

regime_hmm.method: 3-state Gaussian HMM (return + 10d vol), filtered probabilities, numpy Baum-Welch
regime_hmm.expected_remaining_days_note: HMM durations are memoryless: expected remaining time does not shrink as the regime ages.

oos.verdict: Regime labels did NOT separate future returns in the hold-out year: treat the regime as a description of the recent past, not a forecast.

use.BULL: trend-following entries allowed at normal size
use.SIDEWAYS: fewer, smaller entries; favour mean-reversion / defined-risk options
use.BEAR: defensive: no new longs by the swing engine's own rule; hedges / cash

execution.note: Implementation shortfall in basis points vs the decision price (previous close). Positive = cost. Daily-bar TWAP/VWAP are approximations; intraday bars are used when available.

impact.target_note: Official NSE sector indices are used where the free feed has >= 1 year of history; otherwise 'SEC:<sector>' is an equal-weight basket of the scanned Nifty 500 stocks in that sector (not the official index).
impact.method:
Global event -> Indian sector impact map.

1. Sensitivity table (statistics, NOT proven causation):
   For every (global driver, Indian index) pair, an OLS beta of the Indian index's daily return on the driver's move,
   over the last 500 sessions, with t-statistic, R-squared and a stability check (same sign in both halves).
   Timing matters:  drivers that close AFTER the Indian market (US stocks, US yields, VIX, dollar index, Brent, gold)
   are paired with the NEXT Indian session -> usable before the open.  USD/INR trades during Indian hours, so it is
   same-day CO-MOVEMENT (not usable to predict).
2. Shock detector: if a driver's latest move is >= 2 standard deviations, the expected reaction of each linked index is
   beta x move, with a +-1 sd band from the regression residuals. Only links with |t| >= 2.5 and stable sign are used.
3. News linkage: headlines are tagged to drivers by keywords (e.g. "OPEC", "crude" -> Brent) so a shock is shown next
   to the news that may explain it. Keyword tagging is crude and labelled as such.
With ~10 drivers x ~14 indices, some |t| >= 2.5 links can appear by chance (multiple testing); stability filtering reduces this.
